newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin to take over as French premier on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Jospin to take over as French premier on Tuesday.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin will take over from defeated conservative prime minister Alain Juppe on Tuesday at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT), Juppe's office said on Monday.
Jospin announced earlier on Monday that President Jacques Chirac had asked him to form a government following the left's sweeping victory in Sunday's parliamentary election.
Jospin said after meeting Chirac that he planned to form a government "quickly, this week". He said their meeting had been "excellent".
Juppe tendered his resignation to Chirac two hours before Jospin was summoned to the Elysee presidential palace.
He had taken the blame for the first-round defeat of his centre-right coalition and had promised to quit whatever the result of the runoff.
Final results issued on Monday showed the combined left won 318 seats in the 577-member National Assembly, with the 38 Communist members holding the balance of power.
